definitions.document: Leaf area index and solar load measured on the selected obstacles (obstacles, selection), and the geometry of the foliage per planting tray (trays, facade). Weekly, annual and whole-run records only. Every weeks[] and years[] array is dense and aligned with periods.weeks[] and periods.years[]: the record at index i belongs to periods.weeks[i]. A null entry is a period with no reading. The totals of every object are always present; complete says whether any series was dropped for size and omitted lists which.
definitions.periods: weeks: 7-day blocks counted from the local start date, the last one clipped to the run. years: local calendar years, the first and last clipped to the run. Dates are local to meta.timeZone and inclusive. A simulation step is credited to the date of its midpoint.
definitions.coverage: Local dates actually measured. Neither measurement is checkpointed: a resumed run covers only the days after the resume, and the weeks before it are null.
definitions.levels: An obstacle holds surfaces (one per compass orientation and side), each holding height bands. An obstacle's energies are exact; its intensive readings average over orientations, so quote a surface for those. Surfaces on the facade-parallel sides (outer, inner) carry weekly and annual series; rims and returns (edge) and bands carry a total only.
definitions.side: outer: the facade face of the object. inner: a face set back from it - for a planting tray, the back wall seen through the opening, i.e. the tray's projection onto the facade. edge: a rim or return perpendicular to the facade. Both outer and inner face away from the building.
definitions.orientation: Compass sector the surface faces: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW, or up / down when within 30 degrees of horizontal.
definitions.area: m². Total triangle area of the object, every face of a solid included.
definitions.exposedArea: m². The part that can see the sky past the building itself; only it carries readings. A sensor counts in full once at least 4 of 64 hemisphere rays escape the static scene.
definitions.enclosedArea: m². The part whose light-receiving side is walled in by the building and carries no reading.
definitions.daylightHours: h. Hours of the period during which the sky was bright enough to trace. Zero means no reading.
definitions.openSky_kWh_m2: kWh/m². Direct plus diffuse and inter-reflected irradiation the surface would receive with the vegetation removed, summed over the period.
definitions.avoided_kWh_m2: kWh/m². openSky minus what was actually received: the irradiation the vegetation kept off one square metre. Multiply by exposedArea for the energy kept off the whole object. Slightly negative in low sun is physical, when a bright canopy reflects more onto the surface than the sky it hides.
definitions.shadedFraction: 1 - received / openSky, irradiance weighted: the share of the solar gain the greening layer keeps off, i.e. what a building energy model would apply as a shading multiplier. Only the plants shade here - the building's own shadow is removed from both sides of the ratio.
definitions.beamTransmittance: Share of the direct beam that reaches the surface through the foliage, weighted by beam load. Every plant organ blocks the beam.
definitions.diffuseTransmittance: Share of the diffuse and inter-reflected load that reaches the surface.
definitions.leafAreaIndex: m²/m². Total one-sided leaf area per unit surface area, counted along the surface normal up to canopyDepth in front of it, leaves only, through any intervening tray or wall. The classic definition; roughly 2 to 8 for a developed living wall. Mean over the period's daylight hours. Measured with the light model's rectangular leaf proxy - see species.leafOutlineAreaRatio.
definitions.projectedLeafAreaIndex: m²/m². Leaf area PROJECTED onto the surface per unit surface area. Equals leafAreaIndex for leaves parallel to the wall and about half of it for randomly oriented ones.
definitions.leafAreaIndexFromGaps: m²/m². Beer-Lambert inversion of the diffuse gap fraction, -ln(P)/0.93, assuming a spherical leaf angle distribution. What a canopy analyser held in front of the wall would report; falls below leafAreaIndex where leaves clump.
definitions.leafAreaIndexMax: m²/m². Highest per-step value of the period, i.e. the developed canopy rather than its mean. Annual and whole-run records only.
definitions.peakReduction_W_m2: W/m². Largest irradiance the vegetation removed at any moment of the period. The number a peak cooling load wants.
definitions.aggregation: Irradiations are sums over the period. Transmittances and shaded fractions are ratios of those sums, never means of per-step ratios - a plain mean lets a dim step just after dawn count as much as noon. Leaf area indices are means over daylight hours; peaks and maxima are maxima. A year is folded from the same steps as its weeks and the total from the years, so the levels agree.
definitions.trays: The foliage of every plant rooted in each planting tray, surveyed once per local day from the geometry and averaged over the period. Independent of the light model. A tray is the imported object whose soils carry its name with an _S part; a plain field is one tray named field.
definitions.facade: Every tray as one patch: leafArea summed, leafAngleSine and leafDiameter weighted by leaf area over all trays, thickness the largest of any tray. outward is the unit normal of the facade, pointing away from the building, along which the thickness is measured.
definitions.leafArea_m2: m². One-sided area of every blade in the tray, using the species' blade outline, mean over the period's days. Petals are not leaves. Divide by your own facade cell area for a leaf area index; divide by the volume of the vegetation layer for a leaf area density.
definitions.leafAngleSine: Area-weighted mean over the blades of sin(alpha) = sqrt(1 - n_y²), alpha the tilt of the blade from the horizontal and n its unit normal: 0 for horizontal foliage, 1 for vertical. The sine is taken per blade and then averaged, never the other way round.
definitions.leafDiameter_m: m. Area-weighted mean over the blades of 2 sqrt(A / pi), the diameter of the disc with the same one-sided area as the whole blade.
definitions.thickness_m: m. Thickness of the vegetation layer, measured from the tray's back wall outward along the facade normal to the farthest leaf corner, as a bounding box would give it; mean over the period's days. Without a tray mesh it is the canopy height above the seeding level.
definitions.leaves: Mean number of blades. A segmented blade counts once.
definitions.leafAreaMax_m2: m². Largest daily leaf area of the period. Annual and whole-run records only.
definitions.leafAreaFinal_m2: m². Leaf area on the last surveyed day of the period. Annual and whole-run records only.
definitions.thicknessMax_m: m. Largest daily thickness of the period. Annual and whole-run records only.
definitions.days: Daily surveys that contributed to a vegetation record. Zero means no reading.
definitions.width_m, height_m, depth_m: m. Extents of the tray mesh along the facade, vertically, and outward from the back wall. Zero without a mesh.
definitions.species.leafOutlineAreaRatio: One-sided area of the species' blade outline over the rectangle Length x 2 Radius the light model stands a blade in, one factor per blade slice. The tray leaf areas use the outline; the ray-traced leaf area indices use the rectangle, so they read higher by one over this factor.
definitions.precision: Readings are written with four significant digits; coordinates in full.

periods.weekRule: Week i covers the 7 local dates from start + 7i; the last week is clipped to the run.
periods.yearRule: Local calendar years; the first and last are clipped to the run.
